title: Quantitative Imaging of MS2-Tagged hTR in Cajal Bodies: Photobleaching and Photoactivation
protocol: Plate cells on imaging plates the night before the experiment.
In the morning, change media to a live-cell imaging mixture.
Allow cells to equilibrate for an hour or more.
Turn on the stage-top incubator in the meantime.
Allow the temperature to stabilize at 37°C.
Fill the attached water bath with sterile ddH2O.
Turn on CO2 gas as needed.
Take images of TetraSpeck beads to use as a channel registration reference.
Take 20–30 flat field correction slide images.
Focus on cells using the brightfield channel.
Switch to dual camera mode for imaging.
Use Nikon Ti2 Eclipse with CSU-W1 confocal unit and Brukker FRAP module.
Image Cajal bodies (CBs) using mCherry-coilin (excitation 561 nm).
Image hTR using MCP-GFP (488 nm).
Simultaneously image both structures to correct or exclude images for analysis if CB moves during acquisition.
Identify cells where strong hTR signal visibly colocalizes with CBs.
Do not use live camera mode when searching for appropriate cells.
Use the lowest illumination possible.
Take single images using the snap shot function until a desired cell is located.
Define a 2 μm circle around the CB using FRAP software.
Bleach the defined area using the Brukker galvo system with a 405 nm pulse at low laser power (5%).
Set the pixel scan speed to 25 μs per pixel for bleaching.
Ensure the bleach removes about 80% or more of the fluorescence before recovery.
Image after the bleach, starting with a short delay following the bleaching process.
Use an exposure time of 100 ms and take images at intervals of 600 ms for 1 minute.
Take five pre-bleach images to determine baseline fluorescence at a rate of 1/s.
Acquire images of the bleached and imaged cell in a transmitted light channel every 5 to 10 minutes.
Monitor for gross morphological changes, particularly blebbing of membranes and fragmentation of the cell.
Set the total amount of images, laser power, and exposure time to maximize signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
Minimize phototoxicity during imaging.
Minimize acquisition photobleaching.
Ensure that the intensity of a non-FRAP reference region in the cell does not decrease more than 20% over the course of imaging.
Image cells expressing mCherry-coilin and MCP-paGFP on a Zeiss Axio-Observer Z1 Yokogawa CSU-X1 spinning disk inverted confocal microscope.
Position the Cajal body defined with mCherry-coilin in the center of the field of view in Live mode.
Target the centered 1.5 μm diameter area using the Zeiss Direct-FRAP module.
Use a 37°C, 5% CO2 imaging chamber for cell incubation during imaging.
Stabilize lasers (405 nm, 488 nm, and 561 nm) for a minimum of 1 hour before imaging.
Image Cajal bodies using mCherry-coilin with excitation at 561 nm.
Image hTR using MCP-paGFP with excitation at 488 nm.
Capture images sequentially on a single EMCCD camera (Photometrics Evolve 512).
Acquire five pre-bleach images of MCP-paGFP to establish initial conditions.
Set the exposure time for MCP-paGFG to 150 ms with an additional 30 ms camera transfer time.
Expose the 1.5 μm target area to a 405 nm laser at 20% power for 500 ms.
Acquire 195 images following the photoactivation to monitor MCP-paGFP signal for a total of 35 seconds.
Maintain a 20 ms delay between the end of the 405 nm pulse and the start of post-photoactivation imaging.
